title: The python in the hotel hallway and Germans in Buenos Aires
summary: A circus snake act's python escaped, he fainted, and he enjoyed speaking German to Buenos Aires's German community.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Right. Another thing I remember in Buenos Aires -- I stayed at a German hotel there and one of the acts stayed there that was playing at the other theater -- it was a snake act. The guy had big snakes he'd perform with, and I think one of his pythons must have gotten out of the cage, anyhow, the buildings are constructed in South America -- in Buenos Aires -- the hallway is on the outside of the building with a roof over it, but they're attached to the outside of the building. So I had to walk from front of my -- I had the front room -- back to the kitchen. My wife had called me to come and eat my dinner. And as I passed by a room, I hear "pssssss" and I look back and here's the head of this huge python sticking out the transom. WEll, if you want to make me

run into the river or jump off the Empire State Building, just give me a snake, or shake a snake at me -- I'm gone. Well, I backed up against the wall of this outside hall, I hit my head and knocked myself out.
You didn't realize you were backing up so fast.

I hit my head and knocked myself out. They say, when they picked me up the snake was about a foot from me. He had crawled out this transom and in the meantime they went to the theater and got the guy and he put the snake back in. They said I was mumbling something in a foreign tongue they never understood before that. They put water on me and carried me back to the room. I didn't see how far the snake got out, but they said the snake was almost -- he had come out at least four foot and was down over the transom and was coming down the door. He was an 18 foot python. A monster python. Buenos Aires at that time was inhabited by many Germans. There were at least 50,000 Germans, so I was right at home in Buenos Aires. I'd go to the beer halls and speak German and they'd say, 'Are you German?' 'Ja, ich bin ein Deutscher (unintelligible)' And I had a ball in Buenos Aires. I loved it, and especially playing beside the great tango orchestras and they're trying to play jazz and we were playing tango. Had a great time.
